# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Weekly Report (Apr 12 - 18, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on streamlining infrastructure and advancing Layer 2 interoperability components. Significant progress was made in consolidating L2CM (Layer 2 Chain Management) upgrade tasks for `kona-node` and `op-node`, signaling a move toward more unified tracking of protocol upgrades. While the ecosystem expanded with new token integrations on Base, developers also tackled critical stability issues, including a deep dive into flaky peer-to-peer tests and a strategic debate over sequencer redundancy. The overall theme was one of refinement—optimizing CI/CD workflows and finalizing core node functionalities to support the Superchain's growth.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Infrastructure & CI/CD Enhancements
Efforts were directed toward modernizing the project's build environment and deployment security.
*   **Node.js & Publishing:** A new PR ([#1304](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1304)) was introduced to update the Node.js version and configure CI for npm trusted publishing, enhancing the security posture of package releases.
*   **Workflow Migration:** The migration of Docker build workflows to a centralized `images.json` configuration was finalized across several repositories ([#20058](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20058), [#20059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20059), [#784](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/784)), simplifying how container images are managed.

### Ecosystem Expansion (Base Token Listings)
The repository continues to serve as a registry for the growing Superchain ecosystem, with several PRs adding token metadata for assets on the Base network:
*   **Fyrecoin Integration:** Proposals to add Fyrecoin data and the FYRE token ([#1303](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1303), [#1302](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1302)).
*   **AFUK Token:** Addition of AFUK token data on Base ([#1301](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1301)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **L2CM Upgrade Consolidation:** A major cleanup occurred as multiple individual tasks for `kona-node` were consolidated into a single tracking issue. This included work on dev feature flag injection ([#20081](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20081)), gas mechanisms ([#18831](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18831)), and NUT (Network Upgrade Transaction) execution from JSON ([#18836](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18836)).
*   **Op-node Completion:** Work on the `op-node` NUT bundle was officially marked as complete ([#18835](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18835)), representing a milestone in the L2CM project.

### New & Active Issues
*   **P2P Test Flakiness:** Investigation is ongoing into `TestInvalidPayloadThroughCLP2P` ([#19968](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/19968)). The failure involves an assertion error where an invalid payload was accepted but failed to update the block hash correctly. Automated tools have been deployed to isolate the cause within the `memory-all-opn-op-geth` job.
*   **Sequencer Redundancy Strategy:** A technical debate persists regarding support for multiple sequencer RPC endpoints ([#763](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/763)). The current consensus is leaning toward using industry-standard proxies (HAProxy, Nginx) rather than building bespoke failover logic into `op-geth`, prioritizing maintainability over custom client-side features.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by high-level architectural reviews and cross-platform coordination.
*   **L2 Interop Review:** The review of L2 interoperability contracts ([#20008](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20008)) showed strong alignment, though the design of the `CrossL2Inbox` has moved to Slack for deeper synchronous discussion.
*   **Technical Consensus:** The discussion on issue [#763](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/763) highlights a healthy community dynamic where contributors are actively pushing back against "feature creep" in favor of pragmatic, infrastructure-level solutions.
